title: A dispatch of the pages workflow on a branch would publish it to the live site
foundBy: session agent, while adding the site build gate for CUI-074

evidence.verified: `.github/workflows/pages.yml` gives the deploy job `if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'`, so a `workflow_dispatch` from a branch builds the site and stops before publishing it. `actionlint` exits 0 on the workflow at 1244860. The build job it depends on carries no such condition, so a branch dispatch still reports whether the site builds.

details:
`pages.yml` can be started by hand with `workflow_dispatch`, which is the only way to see the site build on a branch. Its `deploy` job carries no condition on the ref. A dispatch from a branch therefore builds that branch and publishes it to the live documentation URL.

Nothing in the workflow says so. The warning has been carried in the handoff notes for this repository instead, as a rule to remember. That is the wrong place for it, because a rule a person has to remember is a rule the next person does not know.

The build job is safe anywhere and worth running on a branch. Only the deploy is not, and a condition on the ref is what separates them.

This was found while adding the site build gate that CUI-074 asked for, which makes dispatching `pages.yml` on a branch unnecessary. The guard still belongs there, because the dispatch button remains and the next person will not know what it does.

notes.text: The guard is in place, and the gate that made the branch dispatch tempting is in the same commit.
